profiles.meeting_scenario: A pediatric academic medical center in Washington, DC is coordinating the next quarter's cross-organization autism access work after publishing early results from its multisystem autism-care initiative. The meeting is between the hospital's developmental-behavioral pediatrics lead and the community coalition's care-navigation manager to align handoffs between hospital referrals, community-based navigation, and shared reporting for a grant update. The agenda is to confirm what families will be routed into the 'navigation pathway,' what counts as a 'closed-loop referral,' which waitlist snapshot will be used in the update, and how equity-focused outreach notes will be incorporated into the shared tracker. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on workflow interfaces, ownership of updates, and what each team will deliver before the end of the month.

members.name: Dr. Elena Ramirez
members.role: Developmental-Behavioral Pediatrician and Hospital Autism Access Initiative Lead
members.expertise: Autism evaluation systems, referral pathway design, quality improvement in pediatric specialty care
members.background: She leads the autism access workstream at a large children's hospital and previously built internal triage protocols to shorten diagnostic delays for Medicaid-insured children.
members.private_state: She wants the grant update to show smoother coordination without creating extra documentation burden for clinic staff, and she is worried that external partners may expect her team to maintain data fields they consider outside the hospital referral workflow.
hidden_assumptions: When a child is placed into the navigation pathway, it means families who already reached the hospital referral queue and were flagged for additional support after internal triage.

A closed-loop referral is achieved once the receiving community organization confirms contact attempts and records a disposition back to the hospital, even if the family has not yet connected to services.
The current waitlist means the live queue length after the most recent monthly triage clean-up, which removes duplicate and unreachable referrals.
Community-facing notes about barriers and social needs can live in the navigator's system and only summarized statuses need to appear in the shared tracker.

members.name: Monique Lee
members.role: Community Care Navigation Manager for the DC Autism Family Access Coalition
members.expertise: Care coordination, cross-agency family navigation, community resource linkage, equity-focused outreach
members.background: She oversees navigators embedded across school, primary care, and family advocacy partners and has spent several years helping families move across fragmented diagnostic and therapy systems.
members.private_state: She wants hospital leadership to recognize navigation as broader than post-referral follow-up, and she is concerned that a narrow hospital definition will undercount coalition work with families facing structural barriers before a specialty referral is complete.
hidden_assumptions: The navigation pathway includes families from the moment a concern is identified by a partner organization, including those who still need referral preparation, insurance troubleshooting, or school documentation before entering the hospital queue.
A closed-loop referral means the family has actually made contact with the next service or completed the intake step, not merely that organizations exchanged status updates.
The current waitlist refers to the last formally reported monthly census used across coalition partners, because that is the stable number suitable for external reporting.
Barrier notes and equity-related outreach details should be entered into the shared tracker so all partners can act on them during handoffs.

misalignment_points.topic: What families are in the navigation pathway
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss routing families into the 'navigation pathway.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means families already in the hospital's autism referral queue who need extra support after specialist triage.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means families identified anywhere in the coalition pipeline, including pre-referral families not yet entered into the hospital queue.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both view navigation as support for families facing barriers, so the phrase sounds naturally shared; the boundary difference is second-order and hidden beneath the same compassionate workflow language.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need a 'closed-loop referral' process.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the loop is closed when the receiving navigation team acknowledges the referral and sends a disposition status back to the hospital.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the loop is closed only when the family has successfully connected to the referred next step, such as completing intake or scheduling with a service.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Closed-loop referral is a familiar quality-improvement phrase in health care, so each assumes the other uses the standard meaning from their own work setting and no one thinks to unpack the operational threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: Which current waitlist number they are using
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the current waitlist' when discussing the grant update and capacity planning.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the live hospital queue after this month's triage reconciliation, which removed duplicates and families no longer seeking services.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the coalition's last published month-end census from the prior reporting cycle, which is the number partners have been using in briefings.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both numbers are recent, both are legitimately current in their respective reporting systems, and in a coordination meeting neither expects the other to be referencing a different snapshot unless a discrepancy becomes numerically obvious.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'add barrier notes to the tracker' so handoffs are smoother.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a short coded summary in the shared hospital-coalition spreadsheet, with detailed outreach and social-context notes kept in the coalition's internal navigation platform.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects navigators to enter substantive barrier descriptions and outreach context directly into the shared tracker so any partner can act without checking another system.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the purpose of documenting barriers, and the word tracker sounds singular and concrete; neither realizes the other imagines a different level of detail and storage location.

turns.inner_thought: I need this to sound coordinated and streamlined for the grant update. The safest path is to keep the interface tight around the hospital referral workflow we already control, without opening the door to extra documentation expectations for my clinic team.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time, Monique. I wanted to use today to make sure we're aligned on handoffs for next month's autism access update and on how families are being routed between the clinic and coalition support. If we can leave with a shared workflow and clear owners for the month-end pieces, that'll put us in a good place.

turns.inner_thought: This is a good opportunity to reinforce that navigation starts well before a hospital referral is fully in place. I want the coalition's broader pipeline to be visible in the update, not just the hospital's post-triage subset.
turns.utterance: Absolutely. From our side, capacity is steady right now, and the navigators are ready to keep families moving through the navigation pathway even with the diagnostic delays still being what they are. We've had a lot of families who need a few different touchpoints to keep momentum.

turns.inner_thought: Good. As long as they can keep absorbing the high-barrier cases we flag after weekly triage, the clinic can show better coordination without changing our internal process. I just want confirmation that this handoff remains reliable.
turns.utterance: That's helpful to hear. On our end, the clinic will keep sending high-barrier referrals into the navigation pathway after weekly triage, and I mainly want to confirm that interface is still working the way we expect.

turns.inner_thought: I should make sure she hears navigation as one continuous pipeline, including families who are still trying to get referral prerequisites together through schools, primary care, or insurance. That should broaden the frame without sounding like a disagreement.
turns.utterance: Yes, and we're seeing the pathway help on the earlier side as well. Families are moving through the navigation pathway while they're still getting PCP referrals, school reports, or insurance paperwork together, so from our perspective it's been useful to treat that as the same pipeline.

turns.inner_thought: For reporting, I need an operational endpoint the clinic can use to clear the handoff once navigation has accepted the case and sent status back. We can't wait on every downstream service connection to count progress, or the numbers will stall.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. On the reporting side, I do think we should count a closed-loop referral once navigation receives the case and sends a status back so the clinic can clear the handoff cleanly.

turns.inner_thought: I agree on the importance of closed-loop referral tracking, but for us the loop really matters when the family actually reaches the next step. We can reflect that in our workflow and still sound aligned here.
turns.utterance: I agree completely that a closed-loop referral process is essential. Our team can make sure those loops are tracked through as families complete the next intake step with community services.

turns.inner_thought: The live queue is still too high even after this month's cleanup removed duplicates and families we couldn't reach. I want navigation effort concentrated on the active referrals still sitting in the hospital system, since that's what leadership will look at first.
turns.utterance: The other issue is capacity. With the current waitlist still high, I want to make sure navigation resources are focused on the children who remain active after this month's clean-up.

turns.inner_thought: For the grant narrative, we need to stick with the coalition's last formally reported month-end census because that's the stable number partners have already been using. I don't want the public-facing story shifting based on a newer internal snapshot.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I would just add that when we use the current waitlist in the grant narrative, it should also reflect the coalition's month-end numbers since those are what partners have been citing publicly.

turns.inner_thought: Now I need to pin down documentation in a way that doesn't create chart-like narrative work for clinic staff. A concise shared tracker with summarized barriers is fine; detailed outreach context should stay in their own system.
turns.utterance: Right. And for the handoffs themselves, I think they'll be a lot smoother if we add barrier notes to the tracker, especially around transportation, language access, and insurance issues.

turns.inner_thought: Good—this is where I want shared visibility. If navigators put substantive outreach context and family-specific barriers into the shared tracker after each attempt, any partner can pick up the thread without losing the equity-related details.
turns.utterance: Agreed. The navigators can start putting outreach context and family-specific barrier notes into the tracker after each contact attempt so the handoffs are more actionable.

turns.inner_thought: Weekly case review should only require concise statuses and high-level barrier categories, not pages of narrative. As long as the tracker shows that navigation accepted the referral and sent back disposition updates, my team can use it for the shared report without extra burden.
turns.utterance: That's great. My clinic staff can review the tracker during weekly case review, and I appreciate that navigation will keep the statuses updated for the shared report. That should help us stay on top of the closed-loop pieces without adding a lot of back-and-forth.

turns.inner_thought: I'll have my team continue across the full coalition pipeline, track closure when families truly connect to next steps, bring the month-end coalition waitlist numbers, and populate the shared tracker with detailed barrier context. This sounds like alignment, and I want to keep it moving.
turns.utterance: Perfect. We'll keep the navigation pathway moving, keep the closed-loop referral work moving with it, and pull together the current waitlist and barrier updates for month-end so the grant package reflects the full picture.
